lead: Overland Park plumbing deals with cold winters, clay soil, basements and homes from the 1950s to today. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Overland Park.
risk: frozen pipes, sewer lines cracked by clay soil and basement plumbing
risk_short: frozen pipes, sewer lines and basements
why: North Overland Park has many homes from the 1950s and 1960s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. South Overland Park and Blue Valley were built mostly after 1985.
Most homes have basements with the water heater, sump pit and floor drains. Winter cold freezes pipes near exterior walls, and clay soil moves with the seasons.
water: WaterOne, the water district for most of Johnson County, treats water from the Missouri and Kansas rivers. It is softened at the plant and is moderately hard.
tips: Test your sump pump each spring.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Overland Park, Nall Hills, Indian Creek, Corporate Woods, Deer Creek, Blue Valley and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Overland Park Building Safety Division, and plumbers are licensed through the Johnson County Contractor Licensing program. Kansas has no statewide plumber license.

faq.q: Who licenses plumbers in Overland Park?
faq.a: Kansas has no statewide plumber license. Overland Park and most Johnson County cities use the county's Contractor Licensing program. Ask for the license number before work starts.
